panels.visual: Heinrich Schliemann (Victorian archaeologist with a moustache, hat and spade) in a royal grave pit at Mycenae holding a golden mask up to the sun
panels.caption: In 1876 Schliemann dug up royal graves at Mycenae, full of gold.

panels.visual: A beaten gold face mask with big eyes and a moustache, shining on a velvet cloth, rays of light
panels.caption: Among the gold were face masks beaten from thin sheets of metal.

panels.visual: Schliemann pointing dramatically at the mask with a big speech bubble, comic pose
panels.caption: He is often quoted as saying, I have gazed upon the face of Agamemnon.

speech.speaker: Schliemann
speech.text: I have gazed upon the face of Agamemnon!

panels.visual: A timeline: the mask, labelled 300 years older than any Trojan War, a big red 'NOT AGAMEMNON' stamp, Glauka shaking her head
panels.caption: The mask is about 300 years older than any Trojan War could have been. Perhaps he never said the famous sentence.
